title: What asset allocation is
objectives: Define asset allocation in one sentence.
Explain why the mix comes before fund selection.
body_md:
Asset allocation is deciding what share of a client's money goes into each asset class, based on their goals, time horizon and ability to handle losses. It is the first investment decision, made before choosing any fund.

## An illustrative moderate mix

Equity 50%, debt 40%, gold 10%. Not a recommendation for any client, just the shape of a mix.

## Why it comes first

Research since the 1980s has found that a portfolio's mix explains most of how much its value swings over time. Fund selection matters, but less. Two clients in the same three funds, with different splits, can have completely different experiences.

## What it is not

- It is not a market call. The mix comes from the client's goal, horizon and risk profile.
- It is not one mix for all the money. Each pot gets its own.
- It is not a one-time decision. Markets move the mix, and life changes it.

**The one line to remember:** the best mix is the one the client can stick with through a bad year.
example: Two clients both hold a flexi-cap fund. One has 70% of the money there, the other 25%. Same fund, very different outcomes and very different behaviour in a fall.

The best mix is the one you can stay with through a bad year.

talk_track.title: Welcome to Module 13
talk_track.text: Welcome to Module 13 of the Fund Horizon training series: asset allocation. How a client's money is split between equity, debt, gold and cash usually matters more than which fund they pick. In this module you'll learn what asset allocation is, why mixing assets helps, how to set the right mix for each client, how to keep it on track, and how to handle the behaviour that breaks a good mix.
